videos.description:
It's molting season, which means your backyard birds are "changing their clothes" 🪶 and staying extra hidden because they're more vulnerable to predators right now. Here's how we help ground feeders like cardinals and doves stay safe during this quiet stretch: we bring the ground up to them! This hanging tray feeder is loaded with a Flaming Hot Feast cake, a mini suet ball, and a sprinkle of safflower, then covered for extra safety. Hang it near a tree or bush for a quick escape route and watch them feel right at home.

videos.title: Empty nyjer feeder? Here's the real reason your finches vanished. Moisture gets trapped inside tradi
videos.description:
Empty nyjer feeder? Here's the real reason your finches vanished. Moisture gets trapped inside traditional tube feeders, clumping the seed and growing mold and bacteria finches instinctively avoid. Mesh-sided and sock-style feeders solve this by letting air circulate, so they dry out fast even though they get wet quicker in rain. Add Feeder Fresh to any feeder style to absorb excess moisture, and after a rain shower, flip mesh or sock feeders upside down to resift the seed and dry it out quickly.

videos.title: Heavy Rain Means Your Bird Feeders Need Attention, and Fast
videos.description:
Heavy rain means your bird feeders need attention, and fast. Once seed gets wet and moldy, birds will stop visiting altogether. For tube feeders specifically, a long brush like the one from Songbird Essentials makes all the difference. Everything shown is available at ForTheWildBirds.com under Crinda's Picks. Happy Birding!
